walkthroughs.title: How can central sleep without losing delivery?
walkthroughs.description: Follow custody, hibernation, reconnect and late answers across the existing content.

steps.narration: Find the stored custody row and the point where the sending event ends.
Which facts survive a new object instance? Read the state owner rather than assuming memory survives.
Follow the open socket while the object sleeps.
Now reconnect with a backlog. Watch answers free slots for the next batch.
Compare a closed socket with an open socket whose answer is late. Which one needs an alarm?

walkthroughs.title: Why can't cleanup freeze delivery again?
walkthroughs.description: Compare the old shared failure with isolated units and the long-operation boundary.

steps.narration: Find the cleanup failure and the work it prevented from running.
Follow the failed unit. What still runs, and where is its failure recorded?
Trace a short request to its answer without a job or alarm.
Long operations retain their existing engine. Keep that boundary distinct from short requests.
